subject.title: Add retry logic to OAuth token refresh

question: Which OAuth refresh failures should the shared manager retry, and what total attempt/time budget should apply across built-in and plugin-owned providers?
rationale: Source proves the missing behavior, but current provider hooks do not define a common retryability contract and the acceptable request latency is a product and auth-policy choice.

options.title: Narrow shared retry
options.body: Retry recognized transport, timeout, 429, and 5xx failures within a small total budget while leaving terminal and reused-token handling unchanged.

options.title: Provider-owned classification
options.body: Extend provider refresh hooks to declare retryability and let each provider own its retry policy, accepting a larger compatibility-sensitive API change.

options.title: Retain single-shot refresh
options.body: Keep the current latency and failure semantics and rely on fallback, restart, or re-authentication after transient refresh failure.

recommendation.title: Narrow shared retry
recommendation.body: Retry recognized transport, timeout, 429, and 5xx failures within a small total budget while leaving terminal and reused-token handling unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor introduced the centralized OAuth lifecycle manager and is the strongest history-backed owner for its retry policy.
